name: Marek Kamiński
milestone_by_age_26: Completed his first solo polar expedition to Spitsbergen in 1990, skiing approximately 350 km across the Arctic island.
early_history_summary: Born in Gdańsk, Poland, Kamiński developed a fascination with travel and polar regions from childhood, reading Jules Verne and Shackleton's journals. He began independent travel as a teenager, hitchhiking through Europe and reaching Cuba and Mexico in the mid-1980s while studying philosophy and physics at Warsaw University. In 1990, at age 26, he undertook his first solo polar expedition to Spitsbergen, covering about 350 km on skis.
family_context_summary: Born in Gdańsk and raised in Pomerania; family background not documented in reviewed sources beyond general mention of his upbringing.
primary_early_advantage_tags: self-directed travel, polar fascination, physical endurance
evidence_summary: Kamiński grew up in Gdańsk reading adventure literature and began independent travel as a teenager, hitchhiking through Europe and to Cuba and Mexico. By 1990, at age 26, he completed his first solo polar expedition to Spitsbergen (~350 km on skis), which was a material milestone establishing him as a serious polar explorer. Family financial or domain advantages are not documented; his early expeditions appear self-initiated and self-funded. His later achievements (both Poles in 1995) built on this foundational polar experience.
starting_point: Born in 1964 in Gdańsk, Poland; raised in Pomerania; family background not documented in reviewed sources.
current_position: Active polar explorer and founder of the Marek Kamiński Foundation; reached the South Pole with his son Kay in December 2025 at age 61; resides in Sopot, Poland.

trajectory.event: Completed first solo polar expedition to Spitsbergen, skiing approximately 350 km.
Completed first Polish crossing of Greenland with Wojciech Moskal, covering about 600 km in 35 days.
Reached both the North Pole (with Moskal) and the South Pole (solo) in one year without external assistance, a world first.
Led the first expedition to both Poles with a disabled person, 15-year-old Jan Mela.
Reached the South Pole again with his 18-year-old son Kay as part of the Pole 2 Pole expedition.

name: Gérard Larrousse
category: Racing driver and motorsport team principal
milestone_by_age_26: Won multiple French national rally events including the Lyons-Charbonnières rally by 1965, and was a competitive professional rally driver on the French national scene by age 26.
early_history_summary: Born in Lyon, France, Larrousse began rallying in 1961 at age 21 while studying commerce at business school in Paris. He quickly established himself with rear-engined cars, winning three quality French events by 1964-65 including the Lyons-Charbonnières. By 1966, he was driving for the Ceida NSU team and decided to become a professional racer, placing second in points in a national championship.
family_context_summary: Born in Lyon; studied commerce at the École Supérieure de Commerce in Paris. Family financial background not documented in reviewed sources.
primary_early_advantage_tags: early rallying, French motorsport scene, rear-engined car specialization
evidence_summary: Larrousse began rallying at 21 while a business student in Paris, using Simca and Renault Dauphine cars. By his third year he won three French national events including Lyons-Charbonnières, and by 1966 (age 26) he was driving for the Ceida NSU team and had committed to professional racing. His major international wins (Le Mans 1973-74, Tour de Corse 1969) came later, but he was already a competitive professional driver with notable national wins by 26. Family background is not documented beyond his Lyon origins and business school education.
starting_point: Born in Lyon, France in 1940; studied commerce at the École Supérieure de Commerce in Paris; family background not documented.
current_position: Retired from Formula One team ownership; former F1 team principal and Le Mans-winning driver; turned 80 in 2020.

trajectory.event: Won multiple French national rally events including the Lyons-Charbonnières, establishing himself as a competitive professional rally driver.
Won the Tour de Corse and was hired by the Porsche factory sportscar team.
Won the 12 Hours of Sebring with Vic Elford in a Porsche 917K and the 1000km Nürburgring.
Won the 24 Hours of Le Mans with Henri Pescarolo for Matra-Simca, repeating the victory in 1974.
Founded his own Formula One team, Larrousse, which competed in F1 from 1987 to 1994.

name: Hans Hollein
milestone_by_age_26: Completed Master of Architecture at UC Berkeley in 1960 at age 26, but no material professional milestone (built commission or award) occurred by age 26; his first commission came in 1965 at age 31.
early_history_summary: Born in Vienna in 1934 to a family of mining engineers, Hollein showed early talent for drawing and attended Franz Cizek's Youth Art Classes. He graduated from the Academy of Fine Arts Vienna in 1956, then studied at IIT Chicago and UC Berkeley, completing his M.Arch in 1960. He met Mies van der Rohe, Frank Lloyd Wright, and Richard Neutra during his US studies.
family_context_summary: Born to a family of mining engineers in Vienna; showed early talent for drawing and attended Franz Cizek's Youth Art Classes.
parent_family_domain_summary: Family background in mining engineering; not directly related to architecture but provided a technical/engineering milieu.
evidence_summary: Hollein completed his architectural education by 1960 (age 26) but had no built commission or professional recognition until the Retti candle shop in 1965 (age 31), which brought international attention and the Reynolds Memorial Award in 1966. His Pritzker Prize came in 1985. No material milestone by age 26.

name: Thorbjørn Olesen
milestone_by_age_26: Won his first European Tour title at the 2012 Sicilian Open at age 22, and added a second European Tour win at the 2014 ISPS HANDA Perth International by age 24.
early_history_summary: Born in Hareskovby, Denmark, Olesen turned professional in 2008 at age 18. He progressed through the Nordic Golf League (winning three times in 2009) and the Challenge Tour (winning The Princess in Sweden in 2010) before earning his European Tour card. His breakthrough came with a win at the 2012 Sicilian Open in his debut European Tour season.
family_context_summary: Born in Hareskovby, Furesø Municipality, Denmark; family background not documented in reviewed sources.
primary_early_advantage_tags: early professional turn, tour progression, Danish golf development
evidence_summary: Olesen turned professional at 18 and methodically climbed through the Nordic Golf League and Challenge Tour, winning multiple times before breaking through on the European Tour at 22 with the 2012 Sicilian Open victory. By 24 he had a second European Tour win and a T6 finish at the 2013 Masters. Family background is not documented; his path appears driven by self-directed competitive progression through golf's lower tours.
starting_point: Born in 1989 in Hareskovby, Denmark; family background not documented in reviewed sources.
current_position: Professional golfer on the European Tour and PGA Tour; has won eight European Tour titles; resides in Dubai, UAE; age 36 as of 2025.

trajectory.event: Won his first European Tour title at the Sicilian Open in his debut season.
Finished T6 at the Masters Tournament, his best major championship result.
Won his second European Tour title at the ISPS HANDA Perth International.
Won the Turkish Airlines Open (Rolex Series) and the World Cup of Golf with Søren Kjeldsen.
Won the Italian Open and helped Europe win the Ryder Cup, defeating Jordan Spieth 5&4 in singles.
Won the Thailand Classic, his seventh European Tour title, earning dual PGA Tour membership for 2024.

name: Li Wenliang
milestone_by_age_26: Graduated from Wuhan University School of Medicine in 2011 at approximately age 26; no material independently verifiable milestone by age 26. Fame arrived at age 34 with COVID-19 whistleblowing in December 2019.
early_history_summary: Born in Beizhen, Liaoning, China to former state enterprise workers who lost their jobs in the 1990s layoffs. He attended Beizhen High School and graduated in 2004, then entered Wuhan University School of Medicine in a seven-year combined bachelor's and master's program. After graduation in 2011, he worked at the Xiamen Eye Center before becoming an ophthalmologist at Wuhan Central Hospital in 2014.
family_context_summary: Born to a Manchu family in Beizhen, Liaoning; parents were former state enterprise workers who both lost their jobs in the 1990s wave of layoffs.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources; parents were state enterprise workers without apparent medical or professional domain connections.
evidence_summary: Li Wenliang's fame came entirely from his role as a COVID-19 whistleblower in December 2019 at age 34, when he warned colleagues about SARS-like cases in Wuhan. By age 26, he had just completed medical school at Wuhan University and was beginning his career as an ophthalmologist. No material milestone by age 26; his parents were laid-off state workers, indicating modest family circumstances.

name: Daniela Peštová
milestone_by_age_26: Was an internationally recognized fashion model with major magazine covers (Cosmopolitan, Mademoiselle, Glamour) starting from 1991, and signed with L'Oréal in 1994, all by age 26.
early_history_summary: Born in Teplice, Czechoslovakia, Peštová was discovered at age 19 at a theater in Prague by Dominique Caffin of the Madison Modeling Agency. She won a modeling competition and signed with Madison, then moved to New York in 1992 without speaking English. Her career rapidly took off with covers on Cosmopolitan (January 1991) and Mademoiselle (June 1991), followed by numerous Glamour covers and a L'Oréal contract in 1994.
family_context_summary: Born in Teplice, Czechoslovakia; family background not documented in reviewed sources. She was discovered at a theater in Prague at age 19.
primary_early_advantage_tags: agency discovery, magazine covers, L'Oreal contract, physical appearance
evidence_summary: Peštová was discovered at 19 by a Madison Modeling Agency scout at a Prague theater, won a competition, and quickly landed major magazine covers (Cosmopolitan, Mademoiselle) by 1991. She moved to New York in 1992 and her career accelerated with Glamour covers, a L'Oréal contract (1994), and the Sports Illustrated Swimsuit cover (1995), all before age 26. Family background is not documented; her breakthrough came from being discovered rather than family connections. The post-Cold War opening of Eastern European talent to Western fashion markets was a structural wave she rode.
starting_point: Born in 1970 in Teplice, Czechoslovakia; family background not documented in reviewed sources; discovered at a Prague theater at age 19.
current_position: Former model, best known for Sports Illustrated Swimsuit covers (1995, 2000, 2006) and Victoria's Secret work; living privately with partner Pavol Habera.

trajectory.event: Landed her first major magazine covers including Cosmopolitan (January) and Mademoiselle (June).
Moved to New York without speaking English; career accelerated with multiple Glamour and Cosmopolitan covers.
Signed with L'Oréal as their print model and spokesperson.
Featured on the cover of the Sports Illustrated Swimsuit Issue for the first time.
Named a Victoria's Secret Angel and appeared in the Victoria's Secret Fashion Show.

name: Shannon Lucid
milestone_by_age_26: Was working as a research chemist at Kerr-McGee and had married with a first child by age 26; no material independently verifiable milestone by age 26. NASA astronaut selection came in 1978 at age 35.
early_history_summary: Born in Shanghai, Republic of China to Baptist missionary parents, Lucid was detained by Japanese forces as an infant before repatriation to the US. She earned a private pilot's license after high school, then a BS in chemistry from the University of Oklahoma in 1963. She worked as a teaching assistant, lab technician, and research chemist at Kerr-McGee before returning to graduate school, earning her PhD in biochemistry in 1973. She was selected as a NASA astronaut in 1978.
family_context_summary: Born to Baptist missionary parents in Shanghai; father Joseph Oscar Wells was a missionary and mother Myrtle was a missionary nurse. Family was detained by Japanese forces during WWII before returning to the US.
parent_family_domain_summary: Parents were Baptist missionaries; not directly related to science or aviation but provided an international upbringing and educational emphasis.
evidence_summary: Lucid had an interesting early life as the daughter of missionaries born in Shanghai, and she earned a private pilot's license after high school. However, by age 26 she was a research chemist at Kerr-McGee with a young family, having not yet begun graduate studies. Her PhD (1973) and NASA selection (1978) both came well after age 26. No material milestone by age 26.

name: Nicklas Lidström
milestone_by_age_26: Scored 60 points (11 goals, 49 assists) as an NHL rookie with the Detroit Red Wings in 1991-92, finishing second in Calder Trophy voting and being named to the NHL All-Rookie Team at age 21.
early_history_summary: Born in Krylbo, Sweden, Lidström grew up in Högbo near Avesta and began playing hockey with Skogsbo SK. He moved to Västerås at age 16 to attend the hockey school and play for VIK Västerås HK in the Swedish Elitserien. Drafted 53rd overall by Detroit in 1989, he joined the Red Wings in 1991-92 and immediately made an impact with a 60-point rookie season, finishing second to Pavel Bure in Calder Trophy voting.
family_context_summary: Born in Krylbo, Sweden; family moved to Högbo near Avesta where his father Jan-Erik built a house. Grew up with two older sisters; idolized Börje Salming. Family was working-class; father described Lidström as a rambunctious child.
parent_family_domain_summary: Not documented in reviewed sources; no evidence of family hockey connections. Father Jan-Erik is mentioned in biography but not as a hockey figure.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Swedish hockey school, Västerås IK development, Detroit Red Wings drafting
evidence_summary: Lidström grew up in a small Swedish town and moved to Västerås at 16 to attend the hockey school, playing three seasons in the Elitserien before joining Detroit. His 60-point rookie season at 21 (Calder runner-up, All-Rookie Team) was a clear material milestone. He idolized Börje Salming and benefited from Sweden's hockey development pipeline. Family background shows no hockey connections; his path was driven by the Swedish elite hockey development system and his own talent.
starting_point: Born in 1970 in Krylbo, Sweden; working-class family; father Jan-Erik built a house in Högbo near Avesta; grew up with two older sisters.
current_position: Retired NHL defenseman (2012); 7-time Norris Trophy winner, 4-time Stanley Cup champion, Hockey Hall of Fame inductee (2015); living in Avesta, Sweden with his family.

trajectory.event: Joined the Detroit Red Wings and scored 60 points as a rookie, finishing second in Calder Trophy voting and named to the NHL All-Rookie Team.
Won his first Stanley Cup with the Detroit Red Wings.
Won the Conn Smythe Trophy as playoff MVP and won his third Stanley Cup.
Won Olympic gold with Sweden at the Turin Winter Olympics.
Won his fourth Stanley Cup and became the first European-born-and-trained captain to win the Cup.
Inducted into the Hockey Hall of Fame in his first year of eligibility.

name: Irina Press
milestone_by_age_26: Won Olympic gold in the 80m hurdles at the 1960 Rome Olympics at age 21, and a second Olympic gold in the pentathlon at the 1964 Tokyo Olympics at age 25, setting world records in both events.
early_history_summary: Born in Kharkov, Ukrainian SSR, Irina Press was the younger sister of Tamara Press, also a prominent athlete. Their father was killed fighting in World War II in 1942, and their mother took the daughters to Samarkand where they began training in athletics. In 1957, Irina followed her sister to Leningrad to train under coach Viktor Alekseyev at the Institute of Railway Engineers. She set her first pentathlon world record in 1959 at age 20, then won Olympic gold in the 80m hurdles at Rome in 1960.
primary_leverage_engine: Physical talent and Soviet athletic pipeline
family_context_summary: Born to a Jewish family in Kharkov; father Natan Press was killed fighting in World War II in 1942. Mother took the daughters to Samarkand where they began athletics training. Elder sister Tamara Press was also an Olympic gold medalist.
parent_family_domain_summary: No documented family athletic background; father was a soldier, mother's occupation not documented. The sisters' athletic careers began in Samarkand after wartime evacuation.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Soviet athletic system, sibling partnership, coach Viktor Alekseyev, wartime displacement
evidence_summary: Press lost her father in WWII and was evacuated to Samarkand with her mother and sister, where they began athletics training. She followed her elder sister Tamara to Leningrad to train under renowned coach Viktor Alekseyev. By 20, she set her first pentathlon world record; at 21, she won Olympic gold in the 80m hurdles at Rome. The Soviet athletic pipeline, sibling partnership with Tamara, and access to elite coaching were key advantages. The family faced wartime displacement and loss of their father, creating both adversity and the circumstances that led to their athletic training.
starting_point: Born in 1939 in Kharkov, Ukrainian SSR to a Jewish family; father Natan Press was killed fighting in WWII in 1942; mother evacuated the family to Samarkand.
current_position: Died on February 22, 2004 in Moscow, Russia at age 64; final status: retired Soviet athlete with two Olympic gold medals and 11 world records.

trajectory.event: Set her first world record in the pentathlon (4,880 points), establishing herself as an elite multi-event athlete.
Won Olympic gold in the 80m hurdles at the Rome Olympics, setting an Olympic record in the semifinals.
Won gold in the 80m hurdles and 4x100m relay at the Summer Universiade in Sofia.
Won Olympic gold in the pentathlon at the Tokyo Olympics, setting a world record of 5,246 points.
Won gold in the 60m hurdles at the European Indoor Championships in Dortmund.
Won her last USSR Championship before retiring abruptly when gender verification was introduced in international athletics.
Died on February 22, 2004 in Moscow, Russia.

name: Veselin Topalov
milestone_by_age_26: Won the World Under-14 Chess Championship in 1989 at age 14, became a Grandmaster in 1992 at age 17, and defeated Garry Kasparov at the 1994 Chess Olympiad in his debut at age 19.
early_history_summary: Born in Ruse, Bulgaria, Topalov learned chess from his father at age 8 and quickly established himself as a prodigy. At age 12, he began working with Silvio Danailov, who became his mentor, trainer, and surrogate parent, housing him and dedicating his life to nurturing Topalov's career. Topalov won the World Under-14 Championship in 1989, silver at the World Under-16 in 1990, and became a Grandmaster in 1992. He made his Olympiad debut in 1994, famously defeating Kasparov on board one.
family_context_summary: Born in Ruse, Bulgaria to a modest family; father taught him chess at age 8. Had a difficult childhood. At age 12, mentor Silvio Danailov took him into his apartment, becoming his trainer, surrogate parent, and financial supporter.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father taught him chess at age 8, providing initial domain exposure. Family was modest; no further domain advantages documented.
primary_early_advantage_tags: father taught chess, Danailov mentorship, chess prodigy, total immersion training
evidence_summary: Topalov's father taught him chess at 8, and by 12 he was taken in by Silvio Danailov, who provided total immersion training—housing, feeding, and funding the young prodigy's tournament career. This intensive mentorship produced a World U-14 title at 14, Grandmaster title at 17, and a famous victory over Kasparov at 19. The family was modest; the key advantage was Danailov's extraordinary dedication. Topalov had a difficult childhood but was recognized as a wunderkind early, channeling all energy into chess.
starting_point: Born in 1975 in Ruse, Bulgaria to a modest family; father taught him chess at age 8; had a difficult childhood before being taken in by mentor Silvio Danailov at age 12.
current_position: Former FIDE World Chess Champion (2005-2006); active grandmaster ranked around No. 35 globally; married with two daughters; residing in Bulgaria.

trajectory.event: Won the World Under-14 Chess Championship in Aguadilla, Puerto Rico, and earned the International Master title.
Became a chess Grandmaster and won the tournament in Terrassa.
Made his Olympiad debut in Moscow, defeating Garry Kasparov on board one and leading Bulgaria to fourth place.
Won the FIDE World Chess Championship tournament, becoming world champion.
Lost the world championship reunification match to Vladimir Kramnik.
Challenged Viswanathan Anand for the world championship, losing 6.5-5.5.
Achieved peak FIDE rating of 2816, placing him joint-tenth on the all-time highest-rated players list.

name: Lyubov Panchenko
milestone_by_age_26: Had graduated from the Kyiv School of Applied Arts embroidery department and was working in a tailoring workshop by age 26; no material independently verifiable milestone by age 26. Her artistic career developed in the 1960s and she never exhibited during the Soviet era.
early_history_summary: Born in Yablunka (now part of Bucha, Ukraine), Panchenko graduated from the embroidery department of the Kyiv School of Applied Arts in the late 1950s. She then worked in a tailoring workshop while expanding her artistic interests, including linocut. In 1968, at age 30, she entered the Ukrainian Academy of Printing. In the 1960s she joined the Club of Creative Youth and worked as a fashion designer at the Republican House of Models.
family_context_summary: Born in the village of Yablunka, Ukrainian SSR; family background not documented in reviewed sources.
evidence_summary: Panchenko graduated from a vocational embroidery program and worked in a tailoring workshop by her mid-twenties. Her artistic career—joining the Club of Creative Youth, working as a fashion designer, and entering the Ukrainian Academy of Printing—developed after age 26. She never had an exhibition during the Soviet era and received the Vasyl Stus Prize only in 2001. No material milestone by age 26.

name: Sophie Calle
milestone_by_age_26: Created her first artistic works (Suite Venitienne, The Sleepers) around 1979 at age 25-26, but these were not independently recognized or exhibited as material milestones at that time; her first book was published in 1983 and major recognition came later.
early_history_summary: Born in Paris, France, Sophie Calle is the daughter of contemporary art collector Robert Calle. Her first artistic project, Suite Venitienne (1979), involved following a man she met at a party to Venice and documenting her surveillance. The Sleepers involved inviting strangers to occupy her bed. These early works were created at age 25-26 but were not published or exhibited until later, with the book appearing in 1983.
family_context_summary: Daughter of Robert Calle, a contemporary art collector, providing early exposure to the art world and its networks.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father Robert Calle was a contemporary art collector, giving Calle direct exposure to the art world from childhood.
evidence_summary: Calle created her first artistic works at 25-26 (Suite Venitienne, The Sleepers, 1979), but these were personal projects not yet recognized or exhibited as material milestones at the time. Her first book was published in 1983, and major recognition (Centre Pompidou exhibitions, Venice Biennale representation) came years later. While her father was an art collector providing art-world exposure, no independently verifiable material milestone occurred by age 26. Being conservative, she is marked ineligible.
